section.p: I am applying for the Rust Engineering Lead role at Canonical, as it strongly aligns with my background in Linux-based systems, open source software, and my recent focus on Rust as a strategic language for future system-level platforms.

With more than 25 years of experience designing and evolving distributed systems on Linux, I have worked across the full software stack, from low-level performance-sensitive components to large-scale web and cloud-native platforms. Over the last years, I have actively invested in Rust and WebAssembly through hands-on projects, tooling experiments, and mentoring developers new to the language.

Canonical’s vision of rethinking the foundations of Linux with Rust resonates strongly with my professional trajectory and technical interests. I am particularly motivated by advocating Rust adoption, contributing to upstream open source projects, improving developer tooling, and helping make Ubuntu an outstanding platform for Rust development.

Used to fully remote and distributed collaboration, I value high engineering standards, clear communication, and technical leadership through code reviews, architecture discussions, and mentoring. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute these strengths to Canonical’s teams.
I would be glad to discuss how my experience and motivation could support Canonical’s Rust and open source ambitions.

Kind regards,
Franck Delahaye
